{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOV5s7_c8AAAABiPMSvQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bs-hLzhLouzw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bs-hL", "number": 3, "title": "Build a playable NES emulator in Rust and WebAssembly without bundled ROMs", "body": "## Goal and scope

Build a genuinely playable, browser-based NES emulator from scratch in Rust, using [takahirox/snes-rust](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust) as the architectural, development and UI/UX reference. Adapt its [first playable baseline](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/3), [current browser app](https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/) and [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md) to NES hardware rather than porting SNES-specific emulation logic.

**Do not include built-in ROMs or bundled demo games.** The production app starts with no cartridge inserted and runs only ROMs explicitly selected by the user (or previously imported by that user). No game ROMs, BIOS/firmware, demo ROM downloads or ROM catalog are to be distributed with the app. Test-only fixtures may be generated locally or obtained from audited, pinned, legally usable sources for testing; keep ROM binaries out of the repository and production artifacts. Never upload a user's ROM or save data.

### Deliverables

- [ ] Establish a Cargo workspace with a platform-independent `nes-core`, a thin `nes-wasm` adapter, a native/headless runner and a static browser frontend. Prefer the dependency-light architecture of snes-rust; do not import or wrap an existing NES emulator core.
- [ ] Implement a coherent NTSC NES machine: Ricoh 2A03 (6502-derived CPU with NES-specific behavior), CPU bus and RAM, reset/interrupts, iNES cartridge parsing, PRG/CHR ROM and RAM, nametable mirroring, mapper 0 (NROM) and additional common mappers (e.g. MMC1, UxROM, CNROM, MMC3) as needed by the selected gameplay targets. Report malformed ROMs and unsupported cartridge types explicitly.
- [ ] Implement synchronized CPU/PPU/APU execution, PPU register and memory behavior, background and sprite rendering, scrolling, VBlank/NMI, OAM DMA, controller serial I/O, and NES APU channels (two pulse, triangle, noise and DMC) with game-generated audio. Implement timing, mapper IRQs and DMA interactions needed by the mandatory targets. Avoid game-specific hacks; document unverified hardware behavior.
- [ ] Provide the browser experience of snes-rust adapted to NES: local `.nes` file selection, automatic start after successful insertion, play/pause/reset, cartridge switching, keyboard and standard gamepad controls, responsive touch controls for the NES D-pad/A/B/Start/Select, native 256×240 pixel output with scaling, Pixel/CRT display options, fullscreen, Web Audio with mute/volume, user-gesture activation and hidden-tab suspension. Keep the UI simple, intuitive and accessible. No bundled-game buttons or demo fallback.
- [ ] Remember successfully imported personal cartridges and preferences locally when browser storage is available, allow removal from the local cartridge list, and persist battery-backed PRG RAM per ROM identity across sessions. Preserve recoverable saves on reset and switching; failed/cancelled imports must not replace the current cartridge. Surface storage failures and avoid silently overwriting an existing save after failed restoration.
- [ ] Add deterministic native tests, a bounded headless runner with input replay and diagnostics (CPU state, test result, framebuffer and audio evidence), and real-browser automated tests using the actual Wasm core. Select at least two distinct playable NES homebrew games with documented legal use, and appropriate CPU/PPU/APU/mapper diagnostic tests. Pin and document provenance, license/permission, artifact hashes and build/fetch instructions; do not treat free download or a repository-level license as proof of binary redistribution rights. Generate original diagnostic ROMs from source or bytes in the test harness where suitable. Keep all test ROM outputs ignored and out of deployment.
- [ ] Provide documented setup/build/run/test commands, a README with controls and verified compatibility/limitations, CI for native and browser checks, and a GitHub Pages workflow that deploys only the validated static app from `main`. Use relative asset URLs suitable for the repository's Pages subpath.
- [ ] Treat this as one end-to-end delivery Issue; use coherent incremental PRs with `Related to #N` until complete. A workspace scaffold, CPU-only implementation or static demo alone is not completion.

### Scope boundaries

The first release targets a playable NTSC baseline, not full NES compatibility or cycle-perfect hardware emulation. PAL/Dendy, Famicom Disk System, expansion audio, special controllers, save states, netplay, cheats, and exhaustive mapper coverage are follow-up work unless necessary for a mandatory gameplay target. Commercial ROMs may only be supplied lawfully by users and are not required for automated acceptance. Test-only fixtures are not built-in ROMs.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Build and CI:** From a clean checkout follow the documented setup, then run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo build --locked -p nes-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release`, `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build` and `npm --prefix web test` (after installing the documented browser runtime). All pass; CI runs equivalent gates, and the production build serves the actual Rust/Wasm emulator.
- [ ] **Hardware behavior:** Run the documented deterministic CPU, bus/cartridge, mapper, PPU, timing/DMA, controller and APU regression suites and diagnostic ROMs with explicit timeouts and expected results. Verify instruction/flag/interrupt behavior, mapper bank/mirroring behavior for supported mappers, actual frame output, controller input and non-silent game-generated audio. All mandatory tests pass; record exact commands/results and known remaining deviations.
- [ ] **Playable baseline:** Using the documented audited test inputs, run at least two distinct actual NES homebrew games through the same generic core and real browser Wasm build. For each, replay from reset beyond the title screen, exercise movement or equivalent controller-driven interaction, assert meaningful game-state/frame changes, and run at least five minutes of emulated gameplay with bounded execution and no panic/hang. Verify a reachable level/round/game-state transition; for at least one audio-producing game verify non-silent APU output and functioning browser playback. Record title, ROM hash, mapper, replay commands, expected results and any limitations. A static diagnostic screen is not a substitute for playable gameplay.
- [ ] **Browser lifecycle and controls:** Run automated browser tests covering the initial empty state, file import, invalid/unsupported ROM rejection, cancelled picker, successful cartridge switching, Play/Pause/Reset, keyboard/gamepad/touch input, scaling/Pixel/CRT/fullscreen, mute/volume, audio activation, and hidden-tab suspension/resume. Expected: actual emulated pixels and input-driven changes, no stale audio or stuck controls, no unexpected console errors; unsupported or failed loads preserve the previous cartridge. Use browser automation or deterministic injected input for device APIs rather than requiring a physical device.
- [ ] **Local persistence and privacy:** Run browser tests using isolated profiles and a battery-backed test cartridge to verify reload, ROM-specific save identity, switching/reset, cartridge removal and storage failure/recovery. Expected: saves restore correctly, different ROMs do not share saves, existing saves are not silently lost, and a network request trace shows no uploads or external requests containing ROM contents, filenames or saves.
- [ ] **No built-in ROMs:** Inspect the tracked tree (`git ls-files`), test fixture provenance and generated production artifact (`web/dist`), including scripts, embedded resources and network requests at startup. Expected: no ROM binaries or bundled games in the tracked tree or deployment, no hard-coded demo choices, no embedded game payloads, no automatic ROM downloads; the browser starts empty and requests only app assets until the user explicitly inserts a local cartridge. Generated/fetched test ROMs are test-only, ignored and excluded from deployment.
- [ ] **Documentation and deployment readiness:** Verify README commands/links and compare documented support to actual test evidence. Serve the production artifact locally under a repository-like subpath and run a browser smoke test: HTML/CSS/JS/Wasm load successfully and the local ROM picker works. Inspect the Pages workflow to confirm it deploys only the validated production artifact with scoped permissions. `git diff --check` passes. Record all pre-merge checks and outcomes in the PR; no mandatory human confirmation is required.

## Post-merge verification

- After the complete PR is merged into `main` and this Issue is closed, verify the GitHub Pages workflow succeeds (with Pages configured to use GitHub Actions), and record the successful Actions run and actual public URL (expected: https://takahirox.github.io/nes-rust-neo/).
- Open the published site in a real browser. Expected: static assets and Wasm initialize under the repository subpath without unexpected HTTP/console errors, the app starts without an inserted cartridge or bundled game choices, and an audited test ROM selected locally runs with video, input and audio. Verify no ROM binaries are exposed by the production artifact and no personal ROM/save data is uploaded.
- Record the publication check results in the merged PR or closed Issue. If publication or live-site checks reveal a defect, open a linked follow-up Issue rather than treating publication as a pre-merge gate.
